newsitem.title: USA: December personal incomes post strongest gain in six months.
newsitem.headline: December personal incomes post strongest gain in six months.

text.p: Individual incomes grew at the fastest rate in six months during December, the Commerce Department said on Monday, and strong job growth fuelled brisk spending.
Incomes from wages, salaries and all other sources were up 0.8 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $6.64 trillion after a 0.6 percent November increase, the department said.
Personal spending increased 0.5 percent in December to a rate of $5.27 trillion following a 0.4 percent rise in November, it added.
Incomes posted a solid rise last year, though not as strong a gain as in 1995.
For the full year 1996, personal incomes increased by 5.5 percent, or $337.7 billion, down from a 6.3 percent, or $362 billion, rise in 1995.
The gains in December incomes and spending reflected steady job growth.
"In December, employment, average weekly hours and average hourly earnings all increased," the department noted.
Notwithstanding the increased spending, savings during December rose to 5.4 cents out of each dollar earned from 5.1 cents in November.

Gains in personal income, which includes wages and salaries as well as income from all other sources such as dividends, interest and businesses, are essential for funding consumer purchases, which fuel two-thirds of national economic activity.
Spending on long-lasting durable goods, which includes cars, picked up to an annual rate of $638.1 billion in December from $634.4 billion in November.

Spending on nondurable products like food and paper products rose to $1.57 trillion from $1.56 trillion in November while spending for services was up to $3.05 trillion in December from $3.04 trillion.
Commerce said that private-sector wages and salaries increased $45.5 billion in December, double the $27.4 billion rise posted in November.
Payrolls of manufacturing companies rose $10.6 billion, compared with a far smaller $2.9 billion increase in November.
